$comment: Every designed problem on Rock's Tools > Data Integrity pages (docs/data-integrity.md, issue 2). The data is clean on purpose, so each problem here is named, small, and tied to a Cast story. Emails stay on example.org, phones stay reserved, and addresses come from the pool. Dates count back from the install day. People are Cast Guids, with a name for the reader.

recordDates.$comment: When each person's record was made, which Rock's Pending report and Connection Status Changes report show. A person's record was made on their household's first visit (attendance.started), or for a child born after it, the given number of days after birth. Pending records take the date of the form that made them, below. A Cast household with no first visit takes the date given here by household key, or else the first thing the load writes for it. A record is never made after the first attendance, gift, group membership, request, or note the load writes for the person, and the Cast expectations and an invariant check it.

generated.$comment: Generated households with no first visit. Each month of the history window takes households until its new records reach source-1's rate from the profile, in source-1's months: first households whose first record falls in that month, then households with no record, then households whose first record comes later. The rest were made in the years before the window: at most 12, each year back taking 0.8 of the one after it.

sources.$comment: Every record's Record Source, by the name of Rock's value. A household that first came with a child under 18 checked the child in, and a household of adults filled out the website's connection card. A record made by its first gift, group sign-up, event registration, connection request, benevolence request, login, or workflow takes that form's source. A child born later was added at check-in. A record made before the history window, before its first record, or by a note draws from the earlier mix. A record with nothing else written for it draws from the noRecord mix. Pending records keep their form's source.

pending.$comment: Every Cast person whose record is Pending, and the form that made the record. Rock's web forms make a new person Pending and set the form's Record Source, so staff review the record before it counts. Nobody reviewed these, so Rock's Pending Individuals report lists them.

selfInactivations.$comment: People who chose "I'm no longer involved" on Rock's Email Preferences page and wrote a note. Rock inactivates the person with their reason and note and marks the record Self Inactivated for review. An adult in one family inactivates the whole family, as the page's Allow Inactivating Family setting does by default. Rock's Self Inactivated Individuals report lists them. Each person's household file says inactive, with the same reason.

connectionStatusHistory.$comment: Connection status changes staff made on Cast people, which Rock writes to each person's History and its Connection Status Changes report reads. Each change runs from one status to the next, and the last ends at the person's status in their household file. A record made in the report's date range also shows as a new person.

dataErrors.$comment: Rock's Person Data Error workflow, which staff start from a person's profile with Report Data Error. Rock's workflow gives every report to its admin person, Alisha Marble, and waits for her resolution. Open reports wait in her My Workflows list. A resolved report says what she did, and a fix she made is in the person's History.

photoRequests.$comment: Rock's Photo Request workflow, which staff start from a person's profile. It emails the person a link to upload a photo or opt out. An upload puts the person in Rock's Photo Request group as Pending until staff verify the photo, which makes them Active. An opt-out makes them Inactive. Rock's Verify Photos page lists the Pending ones. Each upload is the person's own photo in the Cast, dated the day they sent it.

sharedEmails.$comment: Married couples who share one email address, as many couples do. Each household file gives both spouses the same email. Rock's Individuals with Duplicate Emails report lists them, and Rock's duplicate finder scores a couple low, because their first names and genders differ, so the Duplicate Finder does not list them.

sharedPhones.$comment: Phone numbers more than one record carries, as real church data has them. Each household file gives the number. Rock's Individuals with Duplicate Phone Numbers report lists every record with a number another record has. Rock's duplicate finder matches a number only between people of the same gender, so none of these makes a pair in the Duplicate Finder.

failedAddresses.$comment: Cast home addresses Rock's address service could not match, because each is a new home on a street too new for its data. Rock left the No Match result and no map point. Alisha checked Location Locked on each, which stops Rock from sending the address to the service again (decision 316), so it stays on Rock's Location Editor under Not Geocoded until someone places the pin. The household files keep each home's true map point from the address pool, which Rock never got.

settings.$comment: Rock's Data Integrity Settings page. Each Data Automation rule is configured the way a church sets it up, and every rule is off (Jon, issue 2 question 1), so Rock's Data Automation job changes no one. Each rule is Rock's own settings class, saved as JSON in its system setting. Where Rock stores a database Id, this file gives the Guid, and the load writes the Id. General keeps Rock's gender auto-fill confidence of 99.9. NCOA's settings are saved with an NCOA run (slice 3).
